prompt: A teacher reports a mean of $70$ but a median of $85$. This suggests there are likely some ___?

choices.label: low outliers (a few very small values)
high outliers (a few very large values)

hint: The mean and median disagree by a lot here. Think about which kind of extreme value drags a mean downward.

hints.title: 🔁 Another angle
hints.text: Try a small class: scores of $85, 85, 90$ and one score of $20$. Compare the mean with the median and see what pulled them apart.
The mean and median disagree by a lot here. Think about which kind of extreme value drags a mean downward.
The mean $70$ is well below the median $85$. A few very small scores would lower the total without changing the middle score much.
The answer is A: there are likely some low outliers, a few very small values.

explanation: Outliers pull the mean toward them but hardly move the median.
Here the mean, $70$, is lower than the median, $85$, so something pulled the mean down.
A few very small values would do that, while large values would push the mean up instead.
So the data likely has low outliers, which is choice A.
